wars.outcome: 'On March 29, 1452, Vladislav openly declared his hostility against his father'; a treaty followed at Pisce on the Piva between 1 and 5 June (1453 by context); no land changed hands.

notes:
Cliopatria problem: the two 'Duchy of Saint Sava' outlines (1453-1467, 1468-1474, both 2,778 km2, bbox 18.78-19.50 E, 42.17-42.89 N) lie in the Montenegrin interior (Onogost region) and do not touch Herzegovina; Herzegovina itself is drawn as the rump of the Kingdom of Bosnia from 1463 to 1481 (8,134 km2). This dossier takes Herzegovina as the duchy's core, uses Cliopatria's outline only as the eastern part, and runs to 1482 rather than 1474. The corrected sub-shapes for 1463-1467 are rough: 'north of Blagaj' is a latitude band over Herzegovina (placeholder for the page's phrase) and 'the eastern part' is Cliopatria's outline plus the Drina towns Foča and Bosnian Podrinje. Pages give no area. Disagreement: the Duchy page says Novi fell December 1481/January 1482 and infobox 1482; the Kingdom of Bosnia page says December 1481.
The 1470 treaty by which Vlatko became an Ottoman vassal (S5) and the Ottoman suzerainty belong in the ottoman-empire dossier (vassal_start with counterpart duchy-of-saint-sava); the 1444 vassalage of Stjepan to Alfonso V of Aragon (S5) concerns no land and is unrecorded. The Duchy was nominally Bosnian: the Kingdom's relation to Herceg Stjepan ('turbulent') is not dated on the pages. Not on the pages: Cetina, Omiš and Počitelj as holdings (S8 names Omiš, Bar in March 1442, the Neretva valley and Novi). Gazetteer names needed: Blagaj, Onogošt, Polimlje, Humska zemlja, Primorje, Konavle, Piva.
